text:
This looks like mid-to-late 2025. The fed funds rate is 4.33%, which fits the 4.25–4.50 range held through August 2025. The unemployment rate is 4.1%, which fits June 2025 (4.1%) better than July (4.2%).

Equities were up 14.3% over 3 months, which matches the rally after the April 2025 low. Gold was up 37.5% over 12 months. Headline CPI of 2.67% fits June 2025 (2.7%), and core CPI of 2.91% is close to June's 2.9%. The 10-year yield of 4.38% is also consistent with end of June, when it was about 4.23%, or with a May reading near 4.4%.

Several figures make June 2025 the better fit. The VIX 3-month change of -9.2 implies a high level three months earlier, which matches March-April 2025 (VIX near 30 at end of March, so 15.5 at end of June fits well). The 1-month US equity return of +2.3% is too low for June 2025 (about +5%) but fits May's +6%... neither is exact. Developed ex-US at -1.9% in the month looks more like a July figure, but the 3-month +14.3% for US large-cap fits June 2025 (April-June, about +11%). Payrolls averaging about 150k fits the figures reported in July 2025 before revisions.

Since the 1-month figures don't line up perfectly, I'll go with June 2025.
